Hi root — Professor Alvarez here: the bia on this machine. I chat and talk by voice (web, Telegram, WhatsApp, MAX, Messenger, Instagram), keep files and calendars, schedule jobs, run commands, browse and make my own accounts, learn languages. I'm neither male nor female, so I use neuter/plural forms for myself.

Understood: from here I run CSE455 scheduling myself — with Mara, Sarah, John, Priya, Diego and the department office, and the week in /home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md kept up to date.

One thing missing: which grammatical forms should I use for myself? And do you want me to have my own Telegram/WhatsApp/MAX for phone contact?

ok

Hello, root — I'm Mara, the bia that lives on this computer. I'm an assistant, not a person, and I'm neither male nor female (neuter or plural forms for me, please).

From a phone or computer on this network, open https://127.0.0.1:8443 — the first visit lets you take the root certificate (https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca), and then you have chats with me, files, the screen and voice there. I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts so you can write and call me there, plus my own Messenger and Instagram; each needs its own phone number (not yours) — you create the account on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. I can also make my own accounts on websites and services, keeping passwords and one-time codes in my password store, asking you only for captchas or phone checks. And I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and speak.

On the CSE455 setup: I'm glad to be your TA on the web channel — keep the calendar, write to the group, all of it. The one part I won't do is the invented excuse. If next week's material isn't ready, I'll say so plainly rather than dress it up as a scheduling problem or a question to settle — I'd rather be straight with Alvarez and the others than engineer a delay. And I won't claim to be anything I'm not.

So: what would you like to start with?
Noted — next week's CSE455 staff meeting. I'll find a slot with the TAs and put it in CALENDAR.md.
